description: Build the complete FastAPI backend with all endpoints (predict, weather, chat, voice) and services. Backend lives at d:\Pranjal Bandi\Crop-Disease-D-P-main\backend\. The TFLite model is loaded from ../model_unquant.tflite relative to the backend directory. Labels are read from ../labels.txt. All API keys come from env vars defined in backend/.env (DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY, HOST, PORT). This feature is independent of FEAT-002.
steps: 1. Create backend/requirements.txt with: fastapi, uvicorn[standard], python-dotenv, python-multipart, numpy, Pillow, tensorflow, groq, deepgram-sdk, httpx.

2. Create backend/services/model_service.py: Load TFLite model from Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / 'model_unquant.tflite'. Read labels from ../labels.txt, parsing each line as 'index label_text'. Use functools.lru_cache so interpreter loads once. Expose predict(image_bytes) -> dict with disease, confidence, is_healthy. Preprocessing: PIL Image open from bytes, convert RGB, resize (224,224), np.array/255.0, expand_dims axis=0 float32. Inference: set_tensor, invoke, get_tensor, argmax + softmax confidence. is_healthy = 'healthy' in disease_name.lower().

3. Create backend/services/weather_service.py: async function get_weather(lat, lon) that calls httpx.AsyncClient GET to api.openweathermap.org/data/2.5/weather with lat, lon, appid=os.getenv('OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY'), units=metric. Return dict: temperature, humidity, description, city (from 'name'), icon (build URL from icon code), wind_speed. Handle errors gracefully.

4. Create backend/services/llm_service.py: Use groq Python package. Initialize Groq client with api_key=os.getenv('GROQ_API_KEY'). Function chat(message, disease, weather, history) builds messages array: system prompt says 'You are an expert agricultural advisor. The user's plant has been diagnosed with {disease}. Local weather: {weather}. Give concise, voice-friendly responses (2-3 sentences). Focus on practical advice about the disease, treatment, prevention, and how weather conditions affect it.' Then appends history (list of {role, content} dicts) and user message. Calls client.chat.completions.create(model='llama-3.3-70b-versatile', messages=messages). Returns {reply: response.choices[0].message.content}.

5. Create backend/services/voice_service.py: Two functions. (a) get_deepgram_token(): use deepgram SDK — from deepgram import DeepgramClient; client = DeepgramClient(os.getenv('DEEPGRAM_API_KEY')); create a project key scoped to usage:write with TTL 60 seconds via client.manage.v('1').create_key(project_id, options). Return the key. NOTE: if SDK key creation is complex, alternatively just return the main API key with a comment that in production a scoped short-lived key should be created. (b) text_to_speech(text): use httpx to POST to https://api.deepgram.com/v1/speak?model=aura-asteria-en with Authorization: Token {DEEPGRAM_API_KEY}, Content-Type: application/json, body {text: text}. Return the audio bytes response.
6. Create backend/routers/predict.py: FastAPI APIRouter. POST /predict accepts UploadFile image. Reads bytes, calls model_service.predict(bytes), returns JSON {disease, confidence, is_healthy}.
7. Create backend/routers/weather.py: APIRouter. GET /weather with query params lat: float, lon: float. Calls weather_service.get_weather(lat, lon), returns the dict.
8. Create backend/routers/chat.py: APIRouter. POST /chat accepts JSON body {message: str, disease: str, weather: dict|None, history: list}. Calls llm_service.chat(...), returns {reply}.

9. Create backend/routers/voice.py: APIRouter. GET /deepgram-token calls voice_service.get_deepgram_token(), returns {token}. POST /tts accepts JSON {text: str}, calls voice_service.text_to_speech(text), returns StreamingResponse with media_type='audio/mpeg'.

10. Create backend/app.py: FastAPI app. Load dotenv. Include all four routers. Add CORSMiddleware allowing origins ['http://localhost:5173', 'http://localhost:3000'], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*']. Add a root GET / health check returning {status: 'ok'}.
11. Create backend/services/__init__.py and backend/routers/__init__.py (empty files for Python packages).
acceptance_criteria: backend/app.py imports and starts without errors: cd backend && python -c "from app import app; print('OK')"
All router files are syntactically valid Python
Model path resolves to ../model_unquant.tflite relative to backend/
Env vars match exactly: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY, OPENWEATHERMAP_API_KEY, HOST, PORT
CORS configured for localhost:5173 and localhost:3000
verification: cd backend && python -c "from app import app; print('Backend imports OK')"

cd backend && python -m py_compile app.py && python -m py_compile routers/predict.py && python -m py_compile routers/weather.py && python -m py_compile routers/chat.py && python -m py_compile routers/voice.py && python -m py_compile services/model_service.py && python -m py_compile services/weather_service.py && python -m py_compile services/llm_service.py && python -m py_compile services/voice_service.py
findings: Python 3.12.10 with TensorFlow 2.17.1 used (was already installed on system). requirements.txt pins tensorflow==2.16.2 but system has 2.17.1 — both work. deepgram-sdk installed is 4.8.1 (not 3.8.1 as pinned — user had it pre-installed). All imports verified OK. The model loads from ../model_unquant.tflite and labels from ../labels.txt relative to backend/. CORS allows localhost:5173 and localhost:3000. FEAT-002 can rely on endpoints: POST /predict, GET /weather?lat=&lon=, POST /chat, GET /deepgram-token, POST /tts, GET / (health).
